name: plan9-libregexp
url: https://github.com/9fans/plan9port/tree/master/src/libregexp (git clone, sparse: src/libregexp, include, src/lib9/utf) + https://swtch.com/plan9port/unix/libregexp9.tgz (downloaded, 13 KB)
commit: plan9port b6564bd96ca189c69e28797738dad56f91eb5967 (2026-08-26). Tarball libregexp9.tgz: files dated 2004/1225 (portdate). All seven .c files are byte-identical between the two (cmp); only two header constants differ: regcomp.h NSUBEXP 32 (tarball) vs 128 (plan9port), regexp9.h Reclass class[16] vs class[128].
files_measured: PRIMARY (plan9port headers): engines/plan9-libregexp/p9p/{regcomp.c,regexec.c,regaux.c} = cmp-verified copies of plan9port/src/libregexp/*.c with plan9port/include/regexp9.h + src/libregexp/regcomp.h and a 6-line stub lib9.h (the tarball's own minimal lib9.h; plan9port's lib9.h pulls in u.h/libc.h/pthread.h which do not exist for arm-none-eabi). Flags: -Ip9p -Iplan9port/include. SECONDARY: libregexp9/libregexp/*.c with the tarball headers. Also measured but EXCLUDED as non-core: regsub.c (136 B M4, substitution helper), regerror.c (73 B, default error hook = write+exit), rregexec.c (674 B) + rregsub.c (140 B) = Rune*-string API variants. Required external helpers from plan9port/src/lib9/utf: rune.c (chartorune) and utfrune.c, measured separately.
per_function_top: Cortex-M4 -Os, engine core (regcomp.c 2155 + regexec.c 738 + regaux.c 340 = 3233 whole files; 3137 after exclusions): regcomp1 604, regexec1 514, evaluntil 336, bldcclass 328, regexec9 224, operator 124, bldcclass.str1.1 120 (error-message strings), _renewthread 100; then _renewmatch 80, _renewemptythread 80, operand 72, nextc 72, popand 64, pushator 60, pushand 40, rcerror 32, cant 32, newinst 28, regcomp9 8. Compile-error message strings total 339 B of the regcomp.c figure. Required UTF-8 helpers (lib9/utf, not in the 3137): chartorune 150 + utfrune 56 = 206 -> 3343 B linked engine. Tarball-header build: 3133 (regexec.c 734 instead of 738). M0+: 3057 (+218 helpers = 3275). x86-64 (Mach-O; per-function from symbol-address deltas): 5026 incl. 339 B __cstring.
excluded_functions: regcomplit9 (8 B M4 / 12 M0 / 20 x86) and regcompnl9 (8 / 12 / 17): alternative-mode API wrappers (literal-string mode, dot-matches-newline mode); _rrenewemptythread in regaux.c (80 / 88 / 129): used only by the Rune-string rregexec API. Whole non-core TUs excluded: regsub.c, regerror.c, rregexec.c, rregsub.c (see files_measured). DEBUG-only dump()/dumpstack() in regcomp.c are #ifdef'd out (0 B). Nothing else in the three core files is test/debug code.
libc_deps: arm-none-eabi-nm -u (Cortex-M4): regcomp.o: chartorune, free, longjmp, malloc, realloc, regerror9, setjmp, strcat, strcpy, strlen. regexec.o: chartorune, utfrune, free, malloc (+ _renewthread/_renewemptythread/_renewmatch from regaux.o). regaux.o: memcpy, memset. utfrune.o: chartorune, strchr. rune.o: none. So: malloc/realloc/free YES (compile: malloc+realloc; exec: heap fallback), setjmp/longjmp YES (compile-error unwinding), strlen/strcpy/strcat/strchr/memcpy/memset YES, plus the lib9 UTF-8 decoder chartorune and utfrune; regerror9 must be supplied by the application (default regerror.c calls write()+exit()).
ram_model: Heap: regcomp9 mallocs sizeof(Reprog) + 6*sizeof(Reinst)*strlen(pattern) = 33344 + 72*len bytes on ARM32 with plan9port headers (Reprog embeds Reclass class[128] of 260 B each) then realloc-shrinks to the used size; with the 2004 tarball headers (class[16]) it is 4224 + 72*len. Compiled program: 12 B per Reinst (max 6 per pattern char), 260 B per character class (Reclass.spans[64] Runes = max 32 ranges). Stack: regexec9 frame is 20640 B (two Relist[LISTSIZE=10] arrays; Relist = inst ptr + NSUBEXP(128) Resub = 1028 B) with plan9port headers, 5288 B with tarball headers; regexec1 +80 B; _renewthread copies a whole Resublist (1024 B) per thread step when ms>1. Heap fallback: when more than LISTSIZE-2 = 8 NFA threads are live at one step, regexec1 returns -1 and regexec2 mallocs 2 x BIGLISTSIZE(250) x sizeof(Relist) = 514000 B (tarball headers: 130000 B), retries, frees; if that malloc fails regexec returns -1 (error, not nomatch). Instrumented run: 21 of 2088 corpus cases hit this fallback. Static state: 468 B bss in regcomp.c (parser stacks NSTACK=20: andstack 160, atorstack 80, subidstack 80, jmp_buf 92, 14 scalars) -> regcomp is not reentrant; regexec is reentrant. Recursion: none of note (operator->operator(CAT) one level; evaluntil is iterative; Pike VM is linear time, e.g. (a*)*b, (a|aa)*b, (x+x+)+y on 40 chars all finish in <0.3 s on the host; timeouts=0). Strings must be NUL-terminated; an end pointer can be passed via match[0].ep.
features_verified:
Read from regcomp.c/regexec.c/regaux.c and probed with the driver. IMPLEMENTED: literal runes (pattern and text are UTF-8 decoded with chartorune; invalid byte -> U+FFFD consuming 1 byte); '.' = any rune except '
' (regcompnl variant: including '
'); '^' and '$' ALWAYS per-line (BOL after any '
' or at string start; EOL before any '
', at NUL, or at the end pointer) - no way to get plain string anchors; '*' '+' '?' greedy; '|' alternation; '(...)' capturing groups (subexpression ids 1..NSUBEXP-1 = 127, tarball 31; nested and repeated groups OK, last iteration wins, e.g. (a|b)* on abab -> group 1 = [3,4]); '[...]' with ranges over code points ([é-ő] works) and '[^...]' negation - a negated class never matches '
'; ranges are sorted/merged at compile time, max 32 ranges per class, max 128 classes per program (tarball 16); '\x' = literal x for ANY x (so \. \* \( \| \[ \- \] \ work as escapes); overall-match semantics: leftmost start, then LONGEST end (_renewmatch keeps the earlier start, then the longer end) - i.e. 'a|ab' on 'ab' -> [0,2], '1*|[^b]' -> longest alternative, unlike Perl/JS; captures come from the thread that produced the longest match; empty pattern matches [0,0]; search-anywhere is native (fast start-char/BOL skip via utfrune); Resub[0].sp/.ep can bound the search region. Error reporting via user-overridable regerror() + longjmp; regcomp returns NULL on error. NOT IMPLEMENTED: \d \w \s \D \W \S   \B \A \Z (all parsed as the literal letter: '\d+' matches 'ddd'); 
 	 \xHH escapes (literal n, t, x); {n,m} / {n} / {n,} bounded repetition ('{' and '}' are literals); lazy quantifiers *? +? ?? (parse as (x*)? etc., i.e. greedy); (?:...) and every other (?...) form (compile error 'missing operand for ?'); case-insensitive flag (none at all; driver emulates ASCII folding); empty alternatives or empty groups 'a|', '(|a)', '()', '||' -> compile error 'missing operand'; unescaped '-' at a class edge '[a-]' '[-a]' -> compile error "malformed '[]'"; ']' as first class char is not a literal ('[]a]' = empty class + 'a]'); POSIX [[:alpha:]] classes; trailing '' is silently dropped; NUL cannot appear in text; parser depth/operator stack limited to NSTACK=20 (21 nested parens -> error 'operand stack overflow'). Case-insensitivity, accent folding, Unicode properties: none.
difftest: Driver: engines/plan9-libregexp/driver.c (38 lines, plain cc, linked with p9p/regcomp.c regexec.c regaux.c + lib9/utf rune.c utfrune.c). Adaptations: regexec9 is natively search-anywhere with captures, so no wrapping of start positions; regerror9 overridden to print 'error' (library default exits the process); -i emulated by ASCII-lowercasing pattern and text in the driver (engine has no flag; byte offsets unaffected); groups 1..31 printed, '-1 -1' when Resub.sp==0. RESULT corpus_seed1 (primary, plan9port headers): cases=2088 checked=2081 pass=1105 fail=976 timeouts=0 group_spans_checked=59. The tarball-header build gives the identical count and identical failure list. Pass composition: of 1202 expected-match cases 542 have the correct span+groups (422 of them with patterns using only syntax Plan 9 supports, 120 coincidental); of 879 expected-nomatch cases 563 agree (173 genuine, 390 coincidental: the pattern contains an unsupported construct that happens to match nothing). Failure classes (each case counted once, in this priority order): MISSING FEATURE 894 = 456 '(?:' non-capturing group (compile error) + 328 backslash classes \d \w \s \b etc. (taken as literal letters -> wrong span or nomatch) + 68 {n,m} (literal braces -> nomatch) + 42 lazy quantifiers (greedy result); SEMANTICS DIFFERENCE 82 = 74 empty alternative/empty group rejected at compile time ('x(a|)y', '(|a)+', '1()?.') + 3 unescaped '-' at class edge rejected + 2 per-line '^'/'$' ('a$' on 'a\nb' matches, '^b' on 'a\nb' matches; Python: nomatch) + 2 capture placement ('(a*)*' on 'b': group 1 unset vs Python [0,0]) + 1 leftmost-longest alternation ('1*|[^b]' -> [0,2] vs [0,0]); BUG 0; TIMEOUT 0. Control subset - the 613 corpus cases whose pattern uses only Plan 9 syntax, no -i, no newline in text: 537 pass, 76 fail (70 empty-alternative errors, 3 class-edge '-' errors, 2 capture placement, 1 leftmost-longest). 212 corpus cases carry -i; they are covered by the lowercasing emulation and fail only for the other reasons above.
caveats: (1) THE number 3137 excludes the UTF-8 decoder the engine cannot link without (chartorune+utfrune, +206 B -> 3343) and excludes regerror (application must supply one) and regsub. (2) RAM is the real problem for nRF52/ESP32, not flash: with current plan9port headers one compiled Reprog is 33 KB (malloc), regexec needs a 20.6 KB stack frame, and any pattern with >8 simultaneous NFA states triggers a 514 KB heap allocation or returns an error; the 2004 tarball headers shrink these to 4.2 KB / 5.3 KB / 130 KB. These are header constants (NSUBEXP, Reclass class[N], LISTSIZE), so a port would tune them, but the design (per-thread copy of all capture slots) is inherently RAM-hungry. (3) Uses malloc/realloc/free and setjmp/longjmp; regcomp has 468 B of static parser state (not reentrant). (4) Match semantics are leftmost-LONGEST with per-line anchors, not Perl/JS leftmost-first; converting to leftmost-first would change regexec1/_renewmatch. (5) -i in the difftest comes from the driver's ASCII lowercasing, not the engine. (6) x86-64 exclusions were computed from Mach-O symbol-address deltas (nm has no sizes); Apple size(1) reports the 752 B bss as 'data'. (7) The rtk-wrapped diff in this environment reported the two regcomp.h/regexp9.h as identical; cmp shows they differ - all numbers above state which header set they use. (8) The sibling 'plan9-0intro' survey result in this scratchpad measured a different Plan 9 tree (2159/736/340) and is not this measurement.
